    package com.nativelocalstorage;import android.content.Context;import android.content.SharedPreferences;import com.nativelocalstorage.NativeLocalStorageSpec;import com.facebook.react.bridge.ReactApplicationContext;public class NativeLocalStorageModule extends NativeLocalStorageSpec {  public static final String NAME = "NativeLocalStorage";  public NativeLocalStorageModule(ReactApplicationContext reactContext) {    super(reactContext);  }  @Override  public String getName() {    return NAME;  }  @Override  public void setItem(String value, String key) {    SharedPreferences sharedPref = getReactApplicationContext().getSharedPreferences("my_prefs", Context.MODE_PRIVATE);    SharedPreferences.Editor editor = sharedPref.edit();    editor.putString(key, value);    editor.apply();  }  @Override  public String getItem(String key) {    SharedPreferences sharedPref = getReactApplicationContext().getSharedPreferences("my_prefs", Context.MODE_PRIVATE);    String username = sharedPref.getString(key, null);    return username;  }  @Override  public void removeItem(String key) {    SharedPreferences sharedPref = getReactApplicationContext().getSharedPreferences("my_prefs", Context.MODE_PRIVATE);    sharedPref.edit().remove(key).apply();  }  @Override  public void clear() {    SharedPreferences sharedPref = getReactApplicationContext().getSharedPreferences("my_prefs", Context.MODE_PRIVATE);    sharedPref.edit().clear().apply();  }}

package dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.reactnative

import android.util.Log
import com.facebook.react.bridge.ReactApplicationContext

class NativeShopBenchModule(reactContext: ReactApplicationContext) :
    NativeShopBenchSpec(reactContext) {

  override fun getName() = NAME

  override fun getApiUrl(): String = BuildConfig.SHOP_API_URL

  override fun markHomeReady() {
    if (!homeReadyLogged) {
      homeReadyLogged = true
      Log.i("SHOPBENCH", "SHOPBENCH home_ready")
    }
  }

  companion object {
    const val NAME = "NativeShopBench"
    @Volatile private var homeReadyLogged = false
  }
}
EOF

package dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.reactnative

import com.facebook.react.BaseReactPackage
import com.facebook.react.bridge.NativeModule
import com.facebook.react.bridge.ReactApplicationContext
import com.facebook.react.module.model.ReactModuleInfo
import com.facebook.react.module.model.ReactModuleInfoProvider

class NativeShopBenchPackage : BaseReactPackage() {

  override fun getModule(name: String, reactContext: ReactApplicationContext): NativeModule? =
      if (name == NativeShopBenchModule.NAME) NativeShopBenchModule(reactContext) else null

  override fun getReactModuleInfoProvider() = ReactModuleInfoProvider {

                name = NativeShopBenchModule.NAME,
                className = NativeShopBenchModule.NAME,
                canOverrideExistingModule = false,
                needsEagerInit = false,
                isCxxModule = false,
                isTurboModule = true,
            )
    )
  }
}

# Building Everbloom (React Native)

Run every command from the project root on a clean checkout.

## Toolchain used

| Tool | Version |
|---|---|
| React Native | 0.88.1 (New Architecture, Hermes; React 19.3.0) |
| @react-native-community/cli | 20.2.0 |
| Node.js / npm | 26.13.0 / 11.20.0 (RN requires Node >= 22.11) |
| Xcode | 26.6 (17F113), iOS 26.5 simulator runtime |
| CocoaPods | 1.16.2 |
| JDK | OpenJDK 21.0.6 (Android Studio JBR) |
| Gradle / Android Gradle Plugin | 9.4.1 / version pinned by RN 0.88.1 |
| Android SDK | compileSdk 37, targetSdk 36, minSdk 24, build-tools 37.0.0, NDK 27.1.12297006 |

Android builds need `ANDROID_HOME` (for example `~/Library/Android/sdk`) and `JAVA_HOME` pointing at JDK 17–21.

## 1. Install dependencies

```sh
npm ci
(cd ios && pod install)
```

`pod install` also runs React Native codegen for the app's native module (`specs/NativeShopBench.ts`).
If you prefer the Gemfile's pinned CocoaPods: `bundle install && (cd ios && bundle exec pod install)`.

## 2. iOS device release build (benchmarked)

Mode: **Release** configuration, `arm64` iOS device SDK (`iphoneos`), optimizations on, Hermes bytecode bundle embedded in the app (no Metro, no dev menu or hot reload).

Signed, with automatic signing for the team in `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM`:

```sh
export DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=XXXXXXXXXX   # your Apple team ID
xcodebuild -workspace ios/Everbloom.xcworkspace -scheme Everbloom \
  -configuration Release -sdk iphoneos -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' \
  -derivedDataPath ios/build -allowProvisioningUpdates \
  DEVELOPMENT_TEAM="$DEVELOPMENT_TEAM" CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Automatic \
  build
```

Without a team (unsigned, compile check):

```sh
xcodebuild -workspace ios/Everbloom.xcworkspace -scheme Everbloom \
  -configuration Release -sdk iphoneos -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' \
  -derivedDataPath ios/build CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO \
  build
```

Resulting app: `ios/build/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/Everbloom.app`

## 3. Install and launch on a connected iPhone

```sh
xcrun devicectl list devices                       # find the device identifier
DEVICE=<device-identifier>
xcrun devicectl device install app --device "$DEVICE" \
  ios/build/Build/Products/Release-iphoneos/Everbloom.app
xcrun devicectl device process launch --device "$DEVICE" --terminate-existing \
  --environment-variables '{"SHOP_API_URL":"http://192.168.1.20:8787/api"}' \
  dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.reactnative
```

Leave out `--environment-variables` to use the default endpoint (`https://apparel-large-catalog.mock.shop/api`).
The app writes `SHOPBENCH home_ready` to the unified log (via `os_log`) once Home has loaded content.

## 4. iOS Simulator build (verification)

Mode: **Release** configuration for the simulator SDK (`iphonesimulator`). This is the most production-like mode React Native supports on the simulator: same optimized native code and embedded Hermes bundle as the device build, no Metro or dev tools.

```sh
xcodebuild -workspace ios/Everbloom.xcworkspace -scheme Everbloom \
  -configuration Release -sdk iphonesimulator -destination 'generic/platform=iOS Simulator' \
  -derivedDataPath ios/build \
  build
```

Resulting app: `ios/build/Build/Products/Release-iphonesimulator/Everbloom.app`

Install and launch on the booted simulator, with an endpoint override:

```sh
xcrun simctl install booted ios/build/Build/Products/Release-iphonesimulator/Everbloom.app
SIMCTL_CHILD_SHOP_API_URL=http://192.168.1.20:8787/api \
  xcrun simctl launch --terminate-running-process booted dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.reactnative
```

Watch for the log marker:

```sh
xcrun simctl spawn booted log stream --predicate 'eventMessage CONTAINS "SHOPBENCH"'
```

## 5. Android release APK

Mode: **release** build type (`assembleRelease`), Hermes bytecode bundle embedded, signed with the debug keystore that ships with the template.

```sh
(cd android && ./gradlew assembleRelease)
```

Resulting APK: `android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk`

The endpoint is a build-time setting. Set the `SHOP_API_URL` environment variable (or pass the Gradle property `-PSHOP_API_URL=…`) when building. Leave it out to use the default endpoint:

```sh
(cd android && SHOP_API_URL=http://192.168.1.20:8787/api ./gradlew assembleRelease)
# or: (cd android && ./gradlew assembleRelease -PSHOP_API_URL=http://10.0.2.2:8787/api)
```

Change the value with `./gradlew clean` first, or Gradle may reuse the old `BuildConfig`. On the emulator, `10.0.2.2` is the host Mac.

Install and launch:

```sh
adb install -r android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk
adb shell am start -n dev.whiskerrs.shopbench.reactnative/.MainActivity
```

## 6. Build modes summary

| Target | Configuration | JS |
|---|---|---|
| iOS device (benchmarked) | Xcode `Release`, `iphoneos` arm64 | Hermes bytecode embedded (`main.jsbundle`) |
| iOS Simulator | Xcode `Release`, `iphonesimulator` | Hermes bytecode embedded |
| Android | Gradle `release` (debug keystore) | Hermes bytecode embedded |

  -configuration Release -sdk iphoneos -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' \
  -derivedDataPath ios/build -allowProvisioningUpdates \

  build
```

Without a team (unsigned, compile check):

  -configuration Release -sdk iphoneos -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' \
  -derivedDataPath ios/build CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO \
  build

```

# Notes

## Dependencies added

The project was created with `npx @react-native-community/cli@20.2.0 init Everbloom --version 0.88.1`. Beyond `react` and `react-native`, the app has two runtime dependencies:

| Package | Version | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `react-native-safe-area-context` | 5.11.1 | Gets safe-area insets for the notch, home indicator and Android edge-to-edge bars. React Native's own `SafeAreaView` is deprecated, and its docs point to this package. The RN 0.88 template already includes it. |
| `react-native-svg` | 15.16.1 | Draws the design's vector icons (home, search, cart, back, plus the stepper's minus/plus and the empty/error glyphs) from the design's SVG paths. React Native has no vector drawing primitive. |

The dev dependencies are the template's tooling (CLI, Babel, Metro, TypeScript, ESLint, Prettier). I removed the template's Jest setup and its `@react-native/new-app-screen` dependency.

Things I deliberately left out:
- **No navigation library.** React Native has no built-in navigator, so `src/navigation.tsx` implements the tab bar and the per-tab stacks with plain views. Every route of every visited tab stays mounted, and only the top route of the active tab is shown (`display: 'none'` hides the rest). This keeps each tab's stack, state and scroll position when switching tabs. Android's hardware back pops the active stack.
- **No in-app browser library.** React Native has no in-app browser, so "Check out" opens `checkoutUrl` in the system browser with `Linking.openURL`, as the spec allows.

## Native code

- `specs/NativeShopBench.ts` is a Turbo Native Module spec (generated by codegen). It is implemented in `ios/Everbloom/RCTNativeShopBench.mm` and in `android/.../NativeShopBenchModule.kt`.
  - `getApiUrl()`: on iOS, returns `ProcessInfo.environment["SHOP_API_URL"]`. On Android, returns `BuildConfig.SHOP_API_URL`, which is set at build time from the `SHOP_API_URL` env var or Gradle property. An empty value means the default endpoint is used.
  - `markHomeReady()`: on iOS, calls `os_log(OS_LOG_DEFAULT, "SHOPBENCH home_ready")` guarded by `dispatch_once`, so it is written once per process in release builds too. Android writes the same line with `Log.i`. Home calls it in an effect after the first render that has loaded content.
- The app has no other logging: no `console.*` calls.
- iOS `Info.plist`:
  - `CADisableMinimumFrameDurationOnPhone = true`
  - `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads = true`, which allows plain HTTP
  - `UIUserInterfaceStyle = Light`
  - portrait only, iPhone only (`TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = 1`)
  - the template's empty location usage string removed
- The launch screen is a plain white storyboard.
- Android manifest:
  - `usesCleartextTraffic="true"`
  - portrait
  - light AppCompat theme, not DayNight, because there is no dark mode
- The app icons are the template defaults (no custom icon).

## Decisions where the spec is silent

- **GraphQL documents.** Each request sends its operation exactly as written in `spec/storefront.graphql`, plus only the fragments that operation uses. GraphQL rejects documents that contain unused fragments, so sending the whole file is not possible.
- **Request timeout.** API requests time out after 15 s, so an unreachable endpoint shows the error state in reasonable time. GraphQL `errors` with no `data`, non-2xx responses, timeouts and network errors all count as failures.
- **"See all"** in the design's Collections header is not shown. The spec does not list it and gives it no destination.
- **Error text.** "Couldn't load products" uses the spec's ASCII apostrophe. The design uses a typographic one.
- **Sale styling.** The sale rule (price in the `sale` color, compare-at price struck through) applies to every product card: Home, Collection, recommendations and search rows. The spec says Collection uses "the same card as Home"; I used the same price rendering everywhere for consistency.
- **Collection screen.**
  - The nav bar is fixed. The description and sort chips scroll with the grid as the list header.
  - Sort chips and collection chips are horizontal scroll rows, because they are wider than the screen.
  - The nav bar first shows the title passed from Home, then the title from the response.
- **Lazy lists.** These use `FlatList` with `windowSize={5}`, `initialNumToRender` 6–8 and `onEndReachedThreshold={1}` (one visible length from the end).
- **Next-page errors.** If loading the next page fails, the list stays and a Retry button (`error-retry`) appears in its footer.
- **Search.**
  - The field is an uncontrolled `TextInput`. With a controlled one, fast automated typing (`typeText`) dropped characters.
  - Requests use the trimmed text. Each response is checked against the current query, and stale ones are discarded.
  - Typing a new query replaces the results with a spinner while the first page loads.
- **Product screen.**
  - The page dots appear only when there is more than one image. Tapping a dot scrolls to that image.
  - Selecting a pill picks the variant whose `selectedOptions` all match the current selection with that one value changed. If no variant matches exactly, it picks the first variant that has the tapped value.
  - "You may also like" is hidden when there are no recommendations.
  - While loading, the screen shows a spinner with the back button. The error state also keeps the back button.
- **Cart.**
  - "Add to cart" switches to the Cart tab only after the mutation succeeds. On failure it stays on the product page and shows an alert.
  - Cart mutations run one at a time. The stepper and Add button are disabled while one is in flight.
  - A network failure during a cart mutation shows an alert ("Couldn't update cart").
  - A response with `cart: null` keeps the current cart and shows the first user error.
  - The variant title shown on a cart line is the API's `title` (for example "XS"), omitted when it is "Default Title".
  - The empty-cart state's "Start shopping" button switches to the Home tab, as in the design.
- **Tab bar.** Tapping the active tab does nothing; it does not pop to root. The cart badge is drawn next to the tab button, not inside it, so XCUITest can see `cart-badge` as its own element.
- **No animations.** Pushing and popping screens are instant, because there is no framework default transition without a navigation library.
- **Variant prices.** No product in the `apparel-large-catalog` mock data has variants with different prices, so switching variants changes the selection but never visibly changes the price. The code shows the selected variant's `price` and `compareAtPrice`.

## Not met / limitations

- The signed device build (`DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` set) could not be checked here, because no Apple team was configured for this run. The unsigned device build (`CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`) and the Simulator build were both built and verified.
- On Android, the endpoint is a build-time setting only (allowed by the spec).
- Android maps `testID` to the view tag / resource-id that React Native sets. Only the iOS identifiers were checked with XCUITest.

The Everbloom app is built in React Native 0.88.1. Every item on the spec's Done checklist passes except the signed device build, which I couldn't run without an Apple team ID. A fresh copy of the project ran every BUILD.md command successfully: dependency install, unsigned iOS device build, iOS Simulator build, and Android APK.

**What was checked on the iOS Simulator (Release build)**, using a throwaway UI test project I wrote outside the repo:
- **Home** loads, and `SHOPBENCH home_ready` appears in the simulator log once per launch.
- **Collection** scrolls to the end of its 84 products, and all four sorts reorder the list.
- **Search** for "linen" loaded results up to number 216 of 224 through infinite scroll. Responses for an old query are thrown away.
- **Product:** the option buttons switch the variant. No product in this catalog has variants with different prices, so the price never visibly changes; the code does show the selected variant's price. A recommendation opens another product page, and the tab bar is hidden on product pages.
- **Cart:**
  - Add to cart switches to the Cart tab with badge 1.
  - The stepper changes the badge and subtotal ($75 → $150 → $75), and reducing to 0 shows the empty cart.
  - Check out opens Safari.
- **Error state:** pointing `SHOP_API_URL` at a dead address shows the error screen. Retry loads Home once the address works (I put a local proxy there to test this).
- **Accessibility identifiers:** all of them were found by the test.

**Android:** the release APK installs and Home loads on the emulator.

**Not verified:** the signed device build with `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM` set. I didn't use the signing identities on this Mac, because that build can register the bundle ID with Apple. The Android identifiers weren't checked with automation.

**Decisions:**
- **No navigation library.** Tabs and per-tab back-stacks are built from plain React Native views, so switching tabs keeps each tab's history and scroll position. Screen changes are instant, with no slide animation.
- **Two added dependencies:** `react-native-safe-area-context` (the built-in safe-area view is deprecated) and `react-native-svg` for the icons.
- **Check out opens the system browser.** React Native has no in-app browser, and the spec allows this fallback.
- **A small native module** reads `SHOP_API_URL` on iOS (a build setting on Android) and writes the log marker through `os_log`.
- **The search field doesn't round-trip its text through React state.** When it did, fast automated typing dropped letters ("jacket" became "jket"), and the benchmark's automation types the same way.

The other choices where the spec was silent are in NOTES.md, including the 15-second request timeout, leaving out the design's "See all" link, and how cart errors are shown.

Files are in the project root:
- `App.tsx`
- `src/`
- `specs/NativeShopBench.ts`
- `BUILD.md`
- `NOTES.md`
